newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 24.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- CITY WINS FIGHT TO KEEP LIFFE The Corporation of London on Monday won a commitment from the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange that it would remain based in the City of London. The decision is seen as a crucial step in the City's battle with Canary Wharf over which site is seen as London's financial headquarters.

-- PANEL REBUKES BZW IN NORTHERN BID BATTLE The Takeover Panel on Monday night delivered a rebuke to Barclays de Zoete Wedd, who are advising Northern Electric, for withholding information that could have affected the hostile bid from CalEnergy. The Panel also rejected the appeal from Northern to reverse the earlier extension of the bid deadline from last Friday to 1pm Tuesday.

-- HSBC SET TO ACQUIRE 20 PER CENT STAKE IN MEXICAN BANK The Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation is close to agreeing a deal to acquire 20 per cent of Mexican bank Grupo Financiero Serfin. However, an announcement before the end of the year was ruled out. Mexican banks cannot by law be overtaken by foreigners, but foreign banks will hold major stakes in four of the top five banks if the current deal succeeds.

-- LABOUR LOOKS TO AID DEVELOPERS OF 'GREEN' CARS The Labour Party, if elected, is planning to set up a partnership with business to promote the development of a 'green' car. The party's environmental spokesperson, Dr Michael Meacher, said although industry, spurred by tougher European environmental standards, was already working on proposals, the government should take a role in 'forcing the pace'.

-- MOT TEST COMPUTERIZED TO CRACK DOWN ON FRAUD The Ministry of Transport testing scheme for the roadworthiness of older cars is to be computerized in an effort to combat fraud. A total of 61,000 blank MoT certificates were stolen last year and an unknown number were forged. The private finance initiative will pay for the overhaul.

-- POST OFFICE PROFIT UP DESPITE STRIKES The Post Office's pre-tax profit and turnover increased in the first half of the trading year, from 170 million pounds stg to September 1995 to 230 million pounds stg a year later. The increase came despite a series of one-day strikes by postal workers.

-- CLARKE LIKELY TO LIFT RATES SOON Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is expected to raise British interest rates again within two months. Minutes from his October 30 meeting with Bank of England governor Eddie George revealed the Chancellor agreed to raise rates by a quarter-point to their current level of 6 per cent. The governor had said that a quarter-point increase may be insufficient and that another may have to soon follow.

-- KINNOCK IN ROW OVER LANDING SLOTS European Union transport commissioner Neil Kinnock has had to delay plans to legalize the buying and selling of airport take- off and landing slots after opposition from the European Commission competition authorities. The authorities believe the trade in slots could distort competition between airlines.

-- BRITISH GAS REVISES MOBIL DEAL British Gas on Monday successfully renegotaited its second 'take or pay' contract with a leading North Sea oil producer, with a deal with the British subsidiary of Mobil of the USA. No value was placed on the deal, but the company said about a fifth of its 'exposed contracts' had been renegotiated. Shares rose 6p to 227.5p.

-- DEUTSCHE BANK LOSES PREMIER CREDIT RATING FROM MOODY'S Credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service on Monday downgraded Deutsche Bank's long-term credit rating from the highest triple-A rating to AA1. The move affects all Deutsche bank subsidiaries, including British investment bank Morgan Grenfell.
